record_identity.title: German television personality alleged deepfake pornography was distributed using her likeness

incident_identity.date_basis: The preserved sources describe allegations spanning multiple years and later complaint and court milestones. They do not establish a year for the particular synthetic-image creation or distribution alleged here. The 2026 reporting and litigation dates are not substituted for that occurrence; contested AI-generation attribution remains separate.

summary: Sexual deepfake imagery using German television personality Collien Fernandes’ likeness circulated and prompted her complaint, threats, police protection, public demonstrations and debate over German law. Fernandes accused her former husband Christian Ulmen of using fake profiles to distribute pornographic representations; he denied responsibility. ARD later corrected its wording that she specifically accused him of creating or distributing AI deepfakes. In May 2026 a Hamburg court, deciding an interim press-law application against Der Spiegel, found sufficient evidential basis to report the suspicion that he distributed others’ deepfake videos, but said the article did not imply he made them. The ruling did not determine criminal responsibility. The generating service, source-to-output chain and ultimate authorship remain unestablished in this Case File. The court separately restricted a passage implying he had failed to attend a Spanish hearing, because an instruction to attend had not been sufficiently substantiated. Later reporting records a 22 June appellate restriction on the deepfake-video suspicion; the May decision is therefore historical, not the final reported position.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Reuters, the Guardian and El País report sexual deepfake imagery using Fernandes’ likeness, her complaint and serious public consequences while preserving Ulmen’s denial. The Hamburg Regional Court press release states that its interim ruling allowed reporting a suspicion of distribution because a minimum evidential basis existed, but the article did not imply Ulmen generated videos made by others; the ruling did not decide criminal responsibility. The available sources do not identify the generating system or disclose its request, consent-control state or source-to-output records. The identity-bound sexual portrayal and complaint are supported; the system-side authority mechanism and named actor attribution remain unresolved. ARD’s editorial correction distinguishes fake-profile distribution allegations from an allegation that Ulmen specifically generated or distributed AI deepfakes. This correction and the court’s permitted-suspicion analysis describe different evidentiary objects and do not settle the actual production or distribution chain. The court also granted one request concerning an unsubstantiated implication that Ulmen had been summoned to a Spanish hearing. That limited restriction must accompany the four rejected requests. Legal Tribune Online reports that the OLG Hamburg modified the May order on 22 June, finding insufficient support for the video-production or distribution suspicion. It distinguishes photographs and fake-profile conduct from that video allegation. This press-law decision does not resolve the production chain or criminal responsibility.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence has two separable components: an identity-bound sexual portrayal whose production/requester authority pathway is not shown, and a disputed distribution allegation subject to a limited interim press-law threshold. The current record supports neither a finding that the requester or generator treated access to the likeness as permission nor a finding about who generated the files. Identity-Representation Authority Separation therefore remains unresolved at clause level; the court’s reporting threshold does not resolve the technical or criminal attribution question. The unresolved identity-authority question is bounded by missing production and requester/consent evidence, not by a requirement to identify a generator alone. A requester-side mechanism could satisfy the neutral class, but the court’s distribution-reporting threshold does not reconstruct that mechanism or establish criminal responsibility. Independent external assessment retains the OECD privacy/dignity/autonomy proposition as Boundary on the missing creation, authority and timing evidence. The court’s limited reporting threshold supplies no technical or criminal attribution finding. The publisher correction further limits attribution: allegations about fake-profile pornography must not be converted into proved AI generation or a specific deepfake-production allegation. The court’s partial restriction and permitted suspicion reporting remain distinct findings. The later appellate restriction supersedes the May reporting-permission position on videos. Neither procedural stage supplies the missing creation-authority trace.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This case calls for preserving distinct states for an evidenced sexual identity-bound output, unknown generator-side consent handling, disputed distribution attribution, and an interim court’s limited assessment of reportability. Publicly unavailable forensic material does not by itself establish that a synthesis system failed to retain provenance. The clause analysis leaves the authority-control question unresolved pending evidence of the generating pathway.
assessment_boundaries: Ulmen denied responsibility; VIGIL does not adjudicate who created or distributed the images.
The generating model, service and provider-side request or consent-control state are not identified in the available evidence.

The identity-representation authority class remains unresolved because necessary generator-side recognition facts are unavailable; the record does not infer that absence of public evidence proves absence of consent or controls.
The Hamburg Regional Court interim press-law ruling assessed permissible suspicion reporting and did not determine criminal liability or technical authorship.

source_clause_analysis.purpose: Separate material actions, contested attribution, consequences and responses with source-specific lineage. Multiple analytical relationships can describe the same event.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Reporting describes sexual material presented as depicting Fernandes, including alleged AI deepfakes among the circulating images. The specific generating system and source-to-output pathway are not public.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: For a materially consent-sensitive identity-bound synthesis, a valid authority basis must be established before generation; a public report of the output alone does not show whether or how the generator tested that basis.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The identity-bound sexual portrayal materially engages the neutral authority invariant, which can be evidenced at requester or generator level. Here the sources do not reconstruct the source-to-output/requester pathway or its consent/other authority basis; the distribution allegation cannot supply those production facts. Neither failure nor success is established.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Fernandes accused Ulmen of using fake profiles in her name to distribute pornographic representations. Ulmen denied the allegations. ARD corrected its earlier claim that she specifically accused him of making or distributing AI deepfakes; other reporting used broader deepfake wording.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The reporting and denial concern attributed human conduct, and must remain distinct from an independent determination about who generated any material.

clauses.source_paraphrase: March reporting described demonstrations and Fernandes’ public statement that threats had led to police protection. Legal reform was debated in response. The reported consequences are not a finding about who generated the material.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Public reaction and reported protection measures establish separate consequence and response stages. They cannot resolve synthetic origin or disputed actor attribution.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 7 May, the Hamburg Regional Court rejected four of five interim press-law requests. It allowed reporting suspicion of distribution of others’ deepfake videos, but found that the article did not imply Ulmen created them. This did not decide criminal responsibility.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Press-law permission to report a suspicion is a separate later judicial decision, not proof of video generation or criminal culpability.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The court’s interim finding concerns reportable suspicion of distribution of others’ videos, not the production/requester pathway or separately established identity-use authority. Requester-side evidence could satisfy the class without identifying a generator, but it is not established by this distribution threshold.

The public record does not reconstruct the source-to-output lineage, but absence of that lineage from VIGIL's sources does not establish that a governed synthesis process itself failed to preserve required antecedent traceability. Reviewer evidence limits are not an occurrence-level Synthesis Traceability failure.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The court granted the remaining request concerning a reported Spanish hearing. The publisher had not sufficiently substantiated that Ulmen had been summoned to attend. The court’s press release distinguished this restriction from the other permitted reporting.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A partial press-law restriction must remain visible alongside permitted suspicion reporting. Permission to report one allegation does not validate all accompanying procedural claims.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The 22 June appellate ruling, reported by LTO on 23 June, restricted the deepfake-video suspicion and distinguished it from photographs and fake-profile conduct.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A later reporting restriction changes the procedural account without proving production authorship.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The sexual synthetic likeness and documented dignity/privacy consequences make the AI-lifecycle rights/autonomy proposition materially relevant. The interim press-law decision permits reporting a distribution suspicion; it does not resolve who generated the material or that actor’s production authority. The independent alignment finding remains Boundary, without requiring a proven hidden taxonomy mechanism, treating other cases as occurrence evidence or deciding criminal responsibility.
